protocol.name: wayland95_shell_v1
protocol.copyright: Wayland 95. This protocol is private to wayland95-compositor and its shell (win95shell); nothing else should use it.

interface.name: wayland95_shell_v1

description.summary: the compositor's link to its desktop shell

interface.description: The desktop's own keys are the shell's to act on (volume, brightness, the power and sleep buttons, Print Screen, Ctrl+Esc and the others below). The compositor catches them before any program sees them and sends them here, but only while a shell is bound: without one they go to the program with the keyboard as usual. Only one client may bind it at a time; a second gets the already_bound error.

entry.name: print
entry.summary: Print Screen: a picture of the whole screen

entry.name: media_play_pause
entry.summary: the Play (or Play/Pause) key: the playing program, through MPRIS

entry.name: click
entry.summary: StickyKeys latched a key; a slow key was accepted

entry.name: high
entry.summary: locked, or a lock key turned on (ToggleKeys)

entry.name: low
entry.summary: unlocked, or a lock key turned off

event.name: tone
event.description: The compositor does StickyKeys, FilterKeys, ToggleKeys and MouseKeys where the keys arrive; the shell makes their sounds.

event.name: shortcut

description.summary: an Accessibility Options shortcut key was used

event.description: Shift five times, right Shift held for eight seconds, Num Lock held for five, Left Alt+Left Shift+Num Lock or +Print Screen (each only if its shortcut is allowed). The shell turns the feature on or off (in settings.ini, which the compositor follows) and says so.

event.name: sticky_modifiers
event.description: For example "Shift" or "Ctrl + Shift (locked)"; empty when none.

entry.name: move
entry.summary: the window follows the pointer until a click

entry.name: size
entry.summary: its bottom right corner follows the pointer until a click

event.name: switcher_entry

description.summary: Alt+Tab: one window for the box

event.description: Alt+Tab is the compositor's (it must work whatever has the keyboard); the shell draws the box. When it starts, every window comes as a switcher_entry, most recently used first, then switcher_show; each further Tab is a switcher_select, and letting go of Alt (or Escape) a switcher_hide. Without a shell, the windows themselves come to the front in turn.

event.name: window_menu
event.description: Right-clicked on its title bar, Alt+Space, or the program asked: Restore, Move, Size, Minimize, Maximize, Close, at x, y (screen coordinates). The choice comes back as window_action.

event.name: primary_output

description.summary: which display is the main one

event.description: The name (wl_output.name: "eDP-1") of the main display, where the taskbar goes: sent when the shell binds, and when it changes (Control Panel > Display, or that display going away).

request.name: end_task

description.summary: End Task: end the program at once

request.description: The taskbar's End Task: the program the window belongs to is killed (it may lose what it hasn't saved; the shell asks first). Never the compositor, the shell or Xwayland.

request.name: list_windows

description.summary: where the windows are, topmost first

request.description: For the screen capture tool's "a window": the windows on screen (not minimized), each as the rectangle it covers, frame included.

event.name: key

description.summary: one of the desktop's keys went down or up

event.description: Each press is followed by its release. The compositor doesn't repeat a held key: the shell does, if it wants to.

interface.name: wayland95_window_list_v1
interface.description: A window event for each window, topmost first, then done. Nothing more is sent; the client destroys it.
